messages:
laura: Quick heads up — starting onboarding for kiran21b (21B) quantized to int4. Canary started and we're hitting OOMs on a subset of microbatches >4. Dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/kiran21b-canary

sam: Which runtime config are you running? batch/microbatch/max_new_tokens?

laura: Defaults from bringup: batch_size=8, microbatch_size=4, max_new_tokens=256. Error shows CUDA OOM during KV alloc on step ~5 of generation. Sample log:
```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory when allocating 1.2 GiB (tried to allocate kv_cache)
  at serve/core/kv_store.cc:482
```

ash: Do you think this is fragmentation or sustained working set growth? Can you attach a heap snapshot?

laura: Heap snapshot indicates many small free slots and scatter in the freelist — looks like fragmentation after repeated prefixing and conversation histories. Eviction isn't trimming early enough (kv_cache_retention_ms default 60000).

infra-bot: deploy/canary #kiran21b-int4: Canary failed — 2/3 hosts reported OOM. See /deploys/3332109876

maria: Also observed a QA regression vs fp16 on the eval harness: +7% perplexity and some instruction-following failures on long-context prompts (>1k tokens). Might be quantization noise in attention softmax tails.

sam: Proposal — quick mitigations to avoid OOMs and isolate quality: 
1) set kv_trim_threshold=0.6 and reduce kv_cache_retention_ms=15000
2) enable slot compactor sweep every 30s (slot_compactor.interval=30s)
3) lower onboarding defaults: max_new_tokens=128 and microbatch_size=2
4) run eval A/B: fp16 vs int4-hybrid vs int4 (preserve OOB layers) on seedset-500

laura: Applying the config to canary now:
```
serving.config:
  batch_size: 6
  microbatch_size: 2
  max_new_tokens: 128
  kv_trim_threshold: 0.6
  kv_cache_retention_ms: 15000
  slot_compactor:
    enabled: true
    interval_s: 30
```

laura: Quick smoke (2k requests) after changes — no OOMs, latency up ~5ms p95, cost +~2%. Canary healthy. However the quality regression still shows on the long-instruction subset.

ash: For quality: try hybrid quant (int4 for FFN, int8 or fp16 for attention weights) or preserve norm/softmax-critical layers in fp16. Also test per-channel scaling and outlier-aware quant (store scale+zero for OOB channels). Numerics in softmax can blow up small tail probs.

maria: I'll run eval jobs: baseline(fp16) -> int4-hybrid -> int4+outlier fp16. Metrics: ppl, instruction-pass@1/3, and semantic-f1. Will post results to the eval dashboard.

sam: If hybrid restores quality within 2-3% of fp16 we can keep conservative onboarding defaults (max_new_tokens=128) and mark model metadata: onboard-defaults: conservative. Also add automatic fallback: if qualityDelta > 3% for critical prompts, route to fp16 pool.

laura: Added canary rollout plan to the onboarding doc and set a temp default of max_new_tokens=128. Will keep the KV trimming and compactor enabled for the canary stage. Next: maria's eval results + infra will try hybrid quant canary. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

maria: FYI running the eval now, ETA ~45m — will ping here with the numbers.

ash: if you hit recurring fragmentation, we should implement a periodic slot-defrag during low-traffic windows (e.g., 3:00 UTC). That helped for yesterbringups.

laura: Noted — scheduling a defrag job for next maintenance window.
